scope: Frozen old Rust checkout; no mutation or runtime reproduction. Root rechecks active checkout and upstream provenance before final attribution.

findings.title: Kitty image continuation frames omit m=1/m=0
findings.reachability: active component path under Kitty image capability
findings.condition: The encoded payload is longer than4000 base64 characters, so encode_kitty produces multiple chunks.
findings.mechanism: terminal_image.rs178–222 splits the payload into4000-character chunks and computes _m, but never serializes that value. The first frame has transmit controls; later frames have empty controls and neither continuation nor final m flags. This does not implement a multi-chunk Kitty transmission.
findings.effect: Images exceeding one encoded chunk can be interpreted as incomplete/independent protocol messages instead of one image.
caller_chain: Image component rendering -> render_image helper -> Kitty serializer.
findings.limits: Source-derived protocol conclusion only; no terminal emission, downloaded image or protocol experiment was performed.
findings.test_boundary: Existing small-image inline fixture at terminal_image.rs500–520 does not cover multiple chunks.

findings.title: Wrapped truecolor style parser consumes six parameters instead of five
findings.condition: Wrapped content contains standard SGR38;2;r;g;b or48;2;r;g;b and style must carry into another row.
findings.mechanism: update_sgr_context at line_diff.rs161–170 requires index+5 and consumes6 parameters. Standard RGB has5 parameters. A normal RGB sequence falls through into unrelated SGR slots; a following extra SGR parameter can be swallowed into the color sequence.
findings.effect: Subsequent wrapped rows lose/corrupt truecolor and may carry unintended attributes. The existing style-isolation feature itself is real.
findings.limits: No rendered terminal experiment; this is not the separate Theme.fg full-reset versus selective-reset design difference (main TUI-001).

findings.title: Exported OSC8 hit testing misparses URL and close sequences
findings.reachability: public library helper; no internal interactive caller established
findings.condition: get_osc8_link_at_column receives ordinary ESC]8;;uri termination syntax, an OSC8 close, or a click column inside a wide glyph.
findings.mechanism: The helper takes payload after the first semicolon rather than the second. A normal open returns ';uri'; closing8;; stores ';' and leaves link state active. Column equality also misses the second occupied cell of a wide glyph.
findings.effect: Callers of this helper receive malformed or stale link targets/hits.
caller_chain: Definition and lib re-export only in the bounded crates search; native primary mouse dispatch does not call this helper.
findings.limits: Do not label this as an observed browser launch, exploitable URL routing or active primary CLI link failure. line_diff.rs181–197 separately handles OSC8 carry correctly.

findings.title: Exported raw Kitty key parser decodes modifier/event parameters incorrectly
findings.reachability: public library parser; primary CLI keyboard path uses Crossterm
findings.condition: Raw CSI-u or extended-key bytes are passed to the exported string parser.
findings.mechanism: keys.rs uses Ctrl1/Shift2/Alt4 without subtracting the protocol offset, drops colon parameters via filter_map, derives event type from the wrong parameter and has additional key-number/ASCII-only assumptions. Its printable decoder does not reject modified/release input.
findings.effect: Raw-helper users can obtain incorrect key identities or printable text. This does not show that all native typing is affected.
caller_chain: Primary terminal reads Crossterm KeyEvent and keybindings matches it directly; decode_kitty_printable_from_str has no observed internal caller beyond definition.
findings.limits: The complete helper and tests were read. No raw terminal injection was run.

findings.title: Exported StdinBuffer loses bracketed-paste markers split across calls
findings.reachability: public library helper; construction found only in inline tests
findings.condition: A paste start or end escape sequence is split between successive process(data) calls.
findings.mechanism: process_with_bracketed_paste searches only the current data argument for full markers at115/139. It retains no partial marker parser. A split end is appended as paste text and does not exit paste state. The batching timestamp is reset at93–95 immediately before checking elapsed at188–196, and no timer flushes delayed data.
findings.effect: Raw-helper users can remain in paste mode or receive unframed chunks. The nominal cap is also not strict for one oversized buffered chunk.
caller_chain: Bounded crates search found StdinBuffer::new/with_options only in inline tests; primary terminal uses Crossterm typed events.
findings.limits: Not evidence that the active CLI's typed bracketed paste is broken. Native Windows console paste batching is a distinct retained implementation.

findings.title: StdinBuffer invokes callbacks while retaining its callback mutex
findings.reachability: public library helper with caller-installed reentrant callback
findings.condition: An event callback re-registers a callback, or re-enters an operation needing a buffer/paste lock held by the emitting path.
findings.mechanism: emit_event at218–222 holds callbacks.lock while invoking each callback. on_event at81–84 requires the same mutex. PasteEnd emission at118–125 and buffered flush/overflow at168–175,203–207 can also retain data locks.
findings.effect: A reentrant callback can deadlock the calling thread.
caller_chain: Public callback API only; no primary CLI StdinBuffer construction established.
findings.limits: Source lock-order proof, not an executed hang. Does not apply automatically to the separate typed terminal input path.

findings.title: Deleting a folded paste can overwrite another stored payload
findings.reachability: active Editor backspace path with registered paste markers
findings.condition: Delete registered marker1 while higher IDs2 and3 remain, and HashMap iteration visits3 before2.
findings.mechanism: remove_paste at421 collects unsorted higher keys, then423–424 removes old and immediately inserts old-1 into the same map. Moving3->2 overwrites payload2; later removing2 moves payload3 again to1. The separate regex pass436–447 decrements each original marker exactly once, leaving rewritten marker2 without its payload.
findings.effect: Previously pasted content is lost and remaining marker expansion no longer matches the user's original text.
caller_chain: Editor backspace over a registered marker -> remove_paste -> mutable HashMap renumber -> document marker rewrite.
findings.limits: Outcome depends on HashMap iteration order; no runtime reproduction claimed. Native removes the selected marker before renumbering, which avoids a separate TS stale-slice issue and should be preserved.
findings.test_boundary: Inline paste deletion fixture2286–2320 only has one moved higher entry2->1; it does not establish collision safety.

findings.title: Word navigation and deletion mix byte cursors with scalar indices
findings.condition: A current line contains multibyte Unicode and a word-move/kill shortcut is applied.
findings.mechanism: editor.rs1052,1071 and1085–1095 pass byte cursor_col into helpers whose indices are Unicode scalar positions, then use returned scalar positions as byte ranges/cursors. For '你' at byte3, backward lookup can index beyond its one-character vector; forward kill from0 obtains1 and drain(0..1) is not a UTF8 boundary.
findings.effect: Normal word editing can panic or leave a cursor inside a code point.
caller_chain: Native hardcoded word shortcuts in Editor.handle_key -> kill_word_backward/forward or cursor_word_left/right -> scalar-index word helpers.
findings.limits: Source-only; ordinary scalar character editing/set_cursor contains separate byte-boundary protection and is not claimed wholly broken.
findings.test_boundary: Word tests1841–1873 are ASCII; multibyte tests2139–2168 cover character operations instead.

findings.title: Character jump advances byte cursor by target width instead of source-character width
findings.condition: A target character's UTF8 width differs from the character at/before the current byte cursor; example line '你x', cursor0, forward target x.
findings.mechanism: jump_to_char computes search_from as cursor_col+target.len_utf8 or subtraction at1131–1133, then directly slices at1141/1143. In the example search_from=1 splits the three-byte '你'.
findings.effect: Character jump can panic on a valid Unicode line; backward search also excludes an immediately preceding target.
caller_chain: Editor.handle_key pending jump state -> jump_to_char on the next plain/Shift character.
findings.limits: Source comment claiming byte safety is contradicted by the actual slice. No shortcut execution or crash reproduction.

findings.title: Native transcript copy ignores selected columns and viewport geometry
findings.reachability: active primary CLI mouse-drag selection/copy path
findings.condition: A real transcript drag selects text at a width other than80, at a scrolled viewport offset, or within columns of a row.
findings.mechanism: Primary mouse-up calls extract_selected_text after a real drag. The helper re-renders the entire chat container at hardcoded width80, ignores both x coordinates and viewport/layout offsets, uses screen y as transcript row indices, then joins entire raw styled lines.
findings.effect: Clipboard content can be wrong rows, full rows instead of selected columns, and include ANSI sequences.
caller_chain: MouseDown/Drag/MouseUp in primary host -> extract_selected_text(chat_container,start,end) -> native clipboard -> selection cleared.
findings.limits: Native drag selection and configurable copy-on-select are implemented; this is a mapping/serialization defect, not absence of selection. Source-only; no clipboard action performed.

not_promoted_to_catalog_here: TS editor overwide-grapheme recursion is a TS defect, not a Rust defect.
Native image dimension/zero-cell-height, empty-loader-frame and completion-transaction findings remain in the full terminal spec/review for coordinator prioritization.
Theme reset differences belong main TUI-001; missing feature parity is not automatically a defect.
